title: Bandwidth Curve Planner: role-level capacity, scope tranches, and roadmap calendar
creator: Maya Zheng
description: Problem: We rely on ad-hoc spreadsheets and tribal knowledge to allocate staffing across cycles. This causes last-minute scope cuts, uneven role-level load, and inconsistent communication of risk to stakeholders. Goal: Build a lightweight planner and visualizations that produce a role-level bandwidth curve, scope tranches (A/B/C) per initiative, and a calendar-aware roadmap export so PMs and Eng leads can make early trade-offs and communicate commit confidence to GO/NO-GO decision owners.
background: Current artifacts: weekly capacity huddle notes, per-project spreadsheets, and Cycle Board in Linear. We lack a consistent mapping between role availability (engineers, infra, data, QA, design), scoped tranches, and an automated rollup of commit confidence for OKR owners. Related initiatives: capacity-simulator (PM-86213) and cycle-capacity-simulator dashboards maintained by Growth PMs.
proposal: Deliver a minimal Cycle Bandwidth Planner MVP with three outputs: 1) role-level bandwidth curve (heatmap) for the cycle, 2) scope tranche recommendations per initiative (A = committed, B = hedgeable, C = stretch), and 3) calendar export (.ics + CSV) annotated with risk windows and key handoffs. Inputs: headcount per role, planned time allocation (percent), known on-call/shadowing blocks, and hard dependencies. Provide an easy UI in Confluence/Drive for PMs to upload or edit, plus a CLI that converts CSV inputs to the planner outputs for automation in planning rituals.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Heatmap correctly computes role availability given inputs and highlights >80% saturation slots. 2) For 8 sample initiatives, planner suggests tranche splits and shows projected commit confidence score (High/Medium/Low). 3) Calendar export imports cleanly into Google Calendar and shows risk annotations. 4) Documentation and a 30-minute walkthrough session scheduled with PMs and Eng leads. 5) Metrics: reduce late-scope-cut incidents by 30% in the next cycle (tracked in retrospective).
tradeoffs:
- Precision vs. speed: MVP will use coarse weekly buckets rather than day-level scheduling to reduce data entry friction.
- Automation vs. control: automated tranche suggestions will be advisory, with PM override preserved.
- Ownership: product team owns UX and acceptance; Eng will provide data transforms and sample scripts.
- Risk of behavior change: teams may overfit to tranche labels; include guardrails in docs.

implementation_notes: Heuristic for tranche assignment: score initiative by critical-path dependency count, customer impact, and engineering effort. Assign A to the top 60% of probability mass by score; B to next 25%; C the rest. Use role saturation threshold of 80% to flag overload. Integration points: - Use headcount exports from HR CSV (weekly snapshot) - Use on-call calendar CSV from PagerDuty - Hook to Console's team-level latency dashboards to identify support-heavy roles during incident-prone windows.

postmortem_metrics:
- number_of_late_scope_cuts: tracked in retrospective (baseline from last 3 cycles).
- planner_adoption_rate: percent of PMs using planner during planning week.
- accuracy_of_tranche_predictions: percent of A items shipped within cycle.
- time_spent_on_planning: minutes per PM before vs after MVP adoption.
notes: Do not expose individual contributor-level data in exports. All outputs must be role-aggregated to respect privacy. For enterprise customers with Dedicated/Private deployments, include an optional field to tag initiatives with compliance sensitivity so resource allocation can account for specialized onboarding needs.
